newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan sets up mark-to-market study group.
newsitem.headline: Japan sets up mark-to-market study group.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) and Justice Ministry have set up a study group to examine legal issues related to the future adoption of mark-to-market accounting measures by corporations, a MOF official said on Wednesday.

Deliberations among the group, composed mainly of MOF and Ministry of Justice officials and scholars, would precede formal discussions by relevant government councils, said the official from the Corporation Finance Division of MOF's Securities Bureau.
The government's Business Accounting Council is expected to finalise a proposal for the adoption of mark-to-market accounting by corporations around June or July of next year, he said.

"We want to discuss, for example, whether actual changes in the commercial code will be necessary to introduce mark-to-market accounting, or whether interpretation of existing laws will be sufficient," the official said.
"By identifying relevant issues beforehand, we hope it will help provide direction to the discussions to be held at government councils," he said.
In Japan, companies currently calculate the value of their holdings in financial products such as stocks and bonds based on the price at the time of purchase, not the current market value.

Mark-to-market accounting calculates the value of a position based on the daily closing price, thereby reflecting unrealised profit or loss on an outstanding position and making it easier for investors to assess profits and losses on a firm's investments.

The MOF official said the study group would aim to help the Business Accounting Council gain a clearer understanding of the adjustments that need to be made with the commercial code before the council unveils a draft proposal in around February or March.
